title: A Witness for the Cipher
premise: Elodie Vane, the reclusive archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent years solving quietly what the police dismiss, and when chorister Maren Osgood vanishes, Elodie finds her diary still receiving entries weeks after her disappearance. Following a cipher hidden in the cathedral's memorial brasses, Elodie uncovers a forged inheritance scheme entwining the bishop's family with her own late mother's name—and realizes the 'dead' witness who could testify is alive and hiding inside the crypt community itself. As the trial date looms and someone begins killing to keep the cipher buried, Elodie must choose between protecting her found family of vergers, bell-ringers, and misfits and exposing the truth that will destroy one of them. In the end she produces the living witness—Maren herself, who faked her death to survive—and testifies at cost to her own invisibility, finding that being seen was the inheritance she never knew she wanted.
about_author: Yara Ashgrove is the pen name of a former parish records volunteer who spent a decade cataloguing cathedral archives in northern England before turning to crime fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet people who notice everything, from a stone cottage shared with an opinionated cat.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Establishes Elodie's invisible life among the cathedral staff as she catalogs the crypt and quietly notes that three recent 'accidents' share an impossible detail: wet shoes on dry nights. Emotional beat: the comfort of being overlooked, and the itch of a pattern no one else sees.

chapters.title: Maren Osgood Is Missing
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. The young chorister fails to appear for evensong; police call it a runaway case. Elodie retrieves Maren's abandoned diary from the choir loft, noticing entries written in two different hands. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility—no one else will look properly.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. The diary continues eleven days past Maren's disappearance, describing places Elodie can verify and one place she cannot: the crypt. Beat: dread curdling into obsession; Elodie breaks her own rule and visits Detective Inspector Sorrel uninvited.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV alternating Elodie/Sorrel. Sorrel reveals the three 'accidents' were closed over her objections, and that Maren's aunt—a solicitor handling the Halloway inheritance—is pressing to declare Maren dead quickly. Beat: wary alliance; two loners recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Brasses and Buried Names
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Deciphering the diary's marginal marks against the memorial brasses, Elodie finds a cipher keyed to donors' names—including her own mother, listed as a beneficiary of an estate she never mentioned. Beat: the past reaching up through the floorboards; personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: The Bell-Ringers' Silence
chapters.summary: POV Elodie among the tower crew, her found family. Old Tom the steeplekeeper warns her off the crypt; someone has been asking about her after hours. Beat: warmth undercut by paranoia—the sanctuary may be watched.

chapters.title: A Death That Fits Too Well
chapters.summary: POV Sorrel. The fourth accident: Maren's aunt falls from the rood screen gallery. Sorrel finds Elodie's name in the aunt's appointment book. Beat: suspicion tightens around Elodie even as they grieve together.

chapters.title: Questioned in Her Own Archive
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Interrogated, Elodie hides the diary and half-truths her way through, lying for the first time in her careful life. Beat: guilt and exhilaration—invisibility requires complicity now.

chapters.title: What Mother Left Me
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Searching her mother's effects, Elodie finds a matching cipher page and learns her mother witnessed something at the cathedral thirty years ago—an earlier death ruled accidental. Beat: generational echo; fury at the dead for their silences.

chapters.title: The Trial Date Is Set
chapters.summary: POV Sorrel. A grand jury convenes on the Halloway estate; without a witness, the forged will stands. Sorrel and Elodie formalize their partnership off the books. Beat: clock starts ticking; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Someone in the Crypt
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Night watch: fresh candle stubs, moved bones, food wrappers behind the Osgood family vault. Someone lives down there. Beat: terror and tenderness—she leaves bread and does not report it.

chapters.title: Tom Knows More Than He Says
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Confronts old Tom; he confesses he's been feeding the crypt dweller for months but swore secrecy to a dying friend. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal within her found family; trust fractures and reforms.

chapters.title: The Cipher Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Full decryption: the brasses encode a list of witnesses to the original murder, each later killed in staged accidents—all except one initial that matches Maren's handwriting. Beat: revelation high; Maren may be alive and is next on the list.

chapters.title: Bishop's Gambit
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Bishop Halloway offers Elodie a funded archive in exchange for handing over 'the documents.' She declines; that night her flat is searched. Beat: temptation refused, safety gone; the hunter becomes the hunted.

chapters.title: Wet Shoes on Dry Nights
chapters.summary: POV Sorrel. Reopening the three cold cases, Sorrel maps every death to a keyholder's access list—narrowing to the verger, Callum, whom Elodie loves like a brother. Beat: dread of the answer they've both been avoiding.

chapters.title: Callum's Alibi
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Callum provides an alibi that checks out—but too perfectly, rehearsed. Elodie realizes he's covering for someone: his son, who inherited debts under the forged will. Beat: heartbreak; love makes liars of everyone.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. In the crypt, Elodie finally meets Maren alive—hiding since witnessing the aunt's first forgery meeting, kept safe by Tom. But Maren refuses to testify while the killer is free. Beat: relief shadowed by stalemate; the witness must be persuaded, not produced.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days to Trial
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Protecting Maren in plain sight disguised as a visiting conservator; the killer strikes again, nearly catching them in the triforium. Beat: siege atmosphere; found family closes ranks around a stranger.

chapters.title: The Confession in the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Cross-referencing the ledger with bell-rope maintenance logs, Elodie proves the killer must be the assistant verger—Callum himself, whose alibi was built on ropes he'd sabotaged. Beat: devastating clarity; the brother figure is the murderer.

chapters.title: Evensong Trap
chapters.summary: POV alternating. They stage a fake crypt discovery during evensong; Callum comes for Maren and is caught between Sorrel and the bell-ringers in the tower. Beat: climax—violence brief and shocking, resolved not by force but by Tom standing in the doorway refusing to move.

chapters.title: A Witness for the Cipher
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. At trial, Maren testifies; the forged will collapses, and Elodie takes the stand to explain the cipher, publicly ending her invisibility. Beat: cost and catharsis—truth costs her anonymity and gains her a self.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: POV Elodie. Aftermath: the crypt unlocked as a memorial archive, Maren apprenticed beside her, Sorrel bringing cold cases to her desk. Beat: resolution—inheritance redefined as what we build together; the archivist steps into the light.
